newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada says no decision yet on PolyGram.
newsitem.headline: Canada says no decision yet on PolyGram.

text.p: A Canadian government spokesman denied on Thursday that a decision had been taken rejecting PolyGram NV's request to be allowed to distribute movies freely in Canada.
Bill Milliken, spokesman for Industry Minister John Manley, who must make the decision, told Reuters: "There has not been a decision. Negotiations are still under way."
The Financial Post reported on Thursday that "sources said PolyGram's request to be allowed to distribute movies freely in Canada has been turned down. An official ruling has not been issued."

PolyGram, 75 percent-owned by Philips Electronics NV, had sought exemption from strict rules intended to protect Canadian film distributors and producers, promising in return to invest heavily in the Canadian film industry.
PolyGram contends that Canada's cultural restrictions have failed to foster a strong Canadian film industry.
The opposition Bloc Quebecois has urged the Liberal government to block PolyGram from distributing independent movies in Canada.
